newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian govt declines comment on SBC report.
newsitem.headline: Austrian govt declines comment on SBC report.

text.p: The Austrian government said on Wednesday it could not deny or confirm a press report that U.S. telecoms firm SBC was in the race for the country's third mobile phone licence, to be auctioned this summer.
Daily Die Presse on Wednesday quoted unnamed sources in the Transport Ministry, which is in charge of the tender, as saying SBC was seeking a way to enter the Austrian telecoms market.
"I can't say anything about this before the offer period closes," said a ministry spokesman.
Bidders have until July 2 to submit their offers. The ministry last week extended the closing date by four weeks, saying some interested parties had been unable to meet the original deadline.

SBC last month lost out against Italy's Stet in the race to take a minority stake in Austria Mobilkom, the mobile communications unit of postal and telecoms monopoly PTA. Stet paid 8.4 billion schillings for the stake.

The only group of bidders that has confirmed an interest in the third mobile phone license is Connect Austria, which groups Austria's Radex-Heraklith, Germany's Viag, GiroCredit bank and unlisted Constantia Privatbank.

Danish telecoms group Tele Danmark earlier this month was reported to be interested in taking a 15 to 20 percent stake in the consortium. The group has confirmed it was eyeing the Austrian tender, but declined to give details.
A consortium of regional utility companies, dominated by lower Austria's EVN, is also expected to submit a bid.

According to media reports, other bidders could include Britain's Orange as well as several companies which lost out in the race for Austria's second mobile phone license in December 1995 -- such as Vodafone, Bell Atlantic, Germany's RWE and Mannesmann.
